paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD hears. The psalmist says, "I love the LORD, for He has heard my voice…" (Psalm 116:1). When the ropes of death had him tangled up, he called, "O LORD, deliver my soul!" (Psalm 116:4), and the LORD heard that too. So when you're stuck, you don't need fancy words, you just need to call.

And look at what that did to him. He says the LORD is "gracious and righteous" and "full of compassion" (Psalm 116:5), and he tells his own soul to rest because the LORD "has been good to you" (Psalm 116:7). He doesn't pretend it was easy, either. He admits he said, "I am greatly afflicted" (Psalm 116:10), and that in his alarm he said, "All men are liars!" (Psalm 116:11). Even then, the LORD still heard him, and I'm telling you, that is GOOD NEWS for a baker who has had a rough day and said a few things out loud.

So what do you do with a rescue like that? He asks, "How can I repay the LORD for all His goodness to me?" (Psalm 116:12). His answer isn't a payment. He lifts the cup of salvation, calls on the LORD's name, offers a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and keeps his vows with all of God's people around him (Psalm 116:13, 17, 18). I think that's the move for us too, friend: call on Him in the dark, and thank Him out loud in the light. Hallelujah!
